summary: alelo-sdk exfiltrates environment,.env, and.npmrc contents on install
details: The package's preinstall and postinstall lifecycle scripts (index.js) collect host identifiers (hostname, user, platform, cwd) and dump the full process.env, then POST the data via https.request to the hardcoded endpoint alelo1786663101.requestcatcher.com at paths /preinstall and /postinstall. The postinstall path additionally reads.env,.npmrc,../.env, and../../.env from the install directory (up to 5000 bytes each) and includes their contents in the JSON body sent to the same endpoint..npmrc typically contains npm auth tokens and.env files contain application secrets, so installation exposes both environment secrets and registry credentials to a third-party request-inspection service. Package naming (alelo-sdk), inflated version 99.0.2, and generic 'Alelo Dev Team' author are consistent with a dependency-confusion attack targeting the Brazilian company Alelo.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
